ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly high-intensity white (approx. 80-85%) with high-contrast low-intensity black margins and focal markings (approx. 15-20%)
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Solid black continuous banding along the trailing edge and distal tips; large contiguous white central fields on both lobes; yellowish-tan amorphous mottling in the upper-central regions; isolated black circular focal spots on the far-left proximal lobe; vertical black lineation extending from the median notch.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped depression with an approximate pixel angle of 40 degrees and a deep vertical bounding box depth relative to the lobe width.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, high-amplitude irregular serration along the entire superior boundary; numerous sharp peaks and valleys creating a jagged linear profile isolated from the grey sky background.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strongly concave curvature sweeping from the median notch upward toward the pointed distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: High-density clusters of circular, high-contrast white calcified structures (barnacles) concentrated on the extreme distal tips of both the left and right lobes; secondary clusters of circular grey scars on the upper right quadrant of the right lobe.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Extensive network of dark, unaligned linear rake marks; primarily horizontal and oblique orientations concentrated around the central axis near the notch and radiating into the white fields of both lobes.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Multiple parallel linear rake marks (likely cetacean tooth rakes) and significant barnacle colonization on the distal margins.
other_distinctive_markers: Pronounced yellowish-brown pigmentation or bio-staining visible in the center of both lobes, contrasting against the primary white ventral surface.
